title: AGC / AGC1 / AGCO / Argentex / Agrify / AGI — Discount, Credit Maturity, Liquidity Risk and Mining Execution V9

notes: Raw Short -> actual Long corrections: AGC 2016, AGC1 2009, AGI 2000.
AGC1 2009 and AGC1 2012 are senior unsecured debt ideas, not common equity ideas.
AGI 2000 is Alliance Gaming Corporation, later Bally Technologies, not Alamos Gold. The SQL company mapping reflects ticker reuse.
AGCO 2015 and Alamos Gold 2014 have usable source-DB horizon performance rows; the other eight ideas do not.
AGC is a leveraged closed-end fund; its return must separate NAV performance, discount change, distributions and leverage.
Argentex's 2025 collapse arose from collateral/margin-call liquidity pressure despite a low-capex brokerage model; IFX's recommended cash consideration was 2.49p/share.
Agrify's 2022, 2023 and 2024 reverse splits compound to a 1-for-3,000 nominal share consolidation, so raw historical and current share prices are not directly comparable.
Alliance Gaming changed its name to Bally Technologies in 2006 and was acquired by Scientific Games in 2014 for $83.30 cash/share; exact 2000-entry IRR is not asserted without complete split history.
Alamos Gold 2014 is judged on its original Turkey/production horizon and failed despite later company evolution through the AuRico merger.
Alamos Gold 2018 is a different mechanism: Young-Davidson lower-mine execution and Island Gold reserve growth; long-run return also includes substantial gold-price beta.

batch_lessons: Closed-end-fund return should be decomposed into NAV return, discount change, distributions and leverage rather than judged by yield alone.
The same consumer-finance issuer can offer different trades at panic and normalization stages; maturity and security identity matter.
Cyclical equity longs can succeed even when peak-margin forecasts are wrong if the trough and inflection are correctly identified.
Low capex does not mean low capital risk: derivatives brokers can require enormous stress liquidity for collateral calls.
Cash on a balance sheet is not excess cash when the business model commits that cash to customer financing and future burn.
Repeated reverse splits are a warning to reconstruct dilution and business-model failure before comparing nominal share prices.
Historical ticker reuse can silently map one company's old ideas to another company; AGI 2000 is Alliance Gaming, not Alamos Gold.
Mining development NAV requires permit and timing probability; a strong balance sheet does not make delayed permits disappear.
Operating-mine bottleneck removal is often easier to verify than greenfield/development optionality.
Long-run commodity-stock returns must separate company execution from macro commodity-price beta.
